body.statement: For arbitrary \(p_1,\ldots,p_m\in\Delta(\mathcal Y)\) and \(q\in\Delta(\mathcal Y)\), there exists a joint law of \((X_1,\ldots,X_m)\) with \(X_a\sim p_a\) and \(\max_a X_a\sim q\) if and only if \(q\in\mathcal C(p_1,\ldots,p_m)\). Every feasible \(q\) admits a finite monotone-residual transport and circle-cover sampler, and every infeasible \(q\) is separated by a violated displayed capacity inequality.
body.justification: This is the exact cross-threshold compatibility result that turns scalar oracle bounds into one attainable law.
body.gap: FanPark2010 Lemma 2.1 gives pointwise sharp bounds for the CDF of the static binary-treatment contrast \(Y(1)-Y(0)\) and explicitly notes that the resulting CDF envelopes need not be uniformly sharp; Artstein1983 gives general selection capacities and LaiRobbins1976 gives an extremal common-marginal construction. Ponomarev2024 Theorem 1 instead finds the smallest nonredundant Artstein collection for a supplied set-valued-prediction correspondence. None states this heterogeneous finite maximum-pmf iff: its closed-form lower-set and singleton-diagonal system characterizes one jointly attainable law across all thresholds and supplies an attaining sampler.
body.consumer: Each decision node in the SMART recursion uses this criterion to propagate an entire continuation-outcome law rather than one threshold endpoint.
